title: p-Block Elements: Groups 15 to 18 (Allotropy, Trends in Reactivity, & Group Chemistry)
syllabus: Group 15 elements (Nitrogen family): Electronic configuration, trends in atomic/ionic radii, ionization enthalpy, electronegativity; Oxidation states and inert pair effect; Anomalous behavior of nitrogen (catenation, multiple bonding); Allotropes of phosphorus (white, red, black); Hydrides, oxides, and oxoacids of nitrogen and phosphorus; Group 16 elements (Oxygen family): Trends in physical properties, anomalous properties of oxygen; Allotropes of sulfur (rhombic, monoclinic, plastic); Oxides, oxoacids of sulfur (sulfurous, sulfuric, peroxodisulfuric, thiosulfuric); Group 17 elements (Halogens): Trends in electronegativity, electron gain enthalpy (F vs Cl anomaly), bond dissociation enthalpy (Cl2 > Br2 > F2 > I2); Anomalous behavior of fluorine; Interhalogen compounds and oxoacids; Group 18 elements (Noble gases): General properties, ionization enthalpies, Bartlett's experiment; Compounds of xenon (fluorides: XeF2, XeF4, XeF6; oxides/oxyfluorides: XeO3, XeOF4, XeO2F2) - preparations, structures, geometries, and hydrolysis

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The correct order of bond dissociation enthalpy for the homonuclear diatomic halogen molecules is:
questions.solution:
The standard bond dissociation enthalpies of halogens are:
- $\text{Cl}_2$: $242.6\text{ kJ/mol}$
- $\text{Br}_2$: $192.8\text{ kJ/mol}$
- $\text{F}_2$: $158.8\text{ kJ/mol}$
- $\text{I}_2$: $151.1\text{ kJ/mol}$
Fluorine has an anomalously low bond dissociation enthalpy compared to chlorine and bromine because of its extremely small bond length ($142\text{ pm}$), which causes substantial electrostatic repulsion between the non-bonding lone pairs on the two adjacent fluorine atoms.
Therefore, the correct decreasing order is:
$$\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{F}_2 > \text{I}_2$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Complete hydrolysis of xenon hexafluoride ($\text{XeF}_6$) produces a colorless solid compound $X$. Compound $X$ and its molecular geometry are:
questions.solution:
Hydrolysis reactions of $\text{XeF}_6$:
- Partial hydrolysis gives oxyfluorides:
$$\text{XeF}_6 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{XeOF}_4 + 2\text{HF}$$
$$\text{XeF}_6 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2 + 4\text{HF}$$
- Complete hydrolysis yields xenon trioxide ($\text{XeO}_3$):
$$\text{XeF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{XeO}_3 + 6\text{HF}$$
$\text{XeO}_3$ is a colorless, explosive hygroscopic solid. Xenon has 8 valence electrons, forming 3 double bonds with oxygen and retaining 1 lone pair:
- Steric number $= 3\ (\sigma\text{ bonds}) + 1\ (\text{lone pair}) = 4 \implies sp^3$ hybridization.
- The molecular geometry is trigonal pyramidal.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The correct order of thermal stability for the hydrides of Group 16 elements is:
questions.solution:
Thermal stability of Group 16 hydrides ($H_2E$) depends directly on the $E-\text{H}$ bond dissociation energy:
1. As the central atom size increases down Group 16 ($\text{O} < \text{S} < \text{Se} < \text{Te}$), the orbital overlap with the small $1s$ orbital of hydrogen becomes progressively less effective.
2. Consequently, the $E-\text{H}$ bond length increases and the bond dissociation enthalpy decreases sharply:
$$\text{H}-\text{O} (463\text{ kJ/mol}) > \text{H}-\text{S} (347) > \text{H}-\text{Se} (276) > \text{H}-\text{Te} (238\text{ kJ/mol})$$
3. Therefore, thermal stability decreases down the group:
$$\text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{H}_2\text{S} > \text{H}_2\text{Se} > \text{H}_2\text{Te}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following allotropes of phosphorus is chemically the MOST reactive and exhibits chemiluminescence (glows in the dark)?
questions.solution:
1. White phosphorus consists of discrete tetrahedral $\text{P}_4$ molecules.
2. The bond angles in the $\text{P}_4$ tetrahedron are compressed to $60^\circ$, departing drastically from the normal $sp^3$ tetrahedral angle of $109.5^\circ$.
3. This introduces severe angular ring strain, making white phosphorus thermodynamically less stable and chemically the most reactive allotrope.
4. It spontaneously ignites in air at $\approx 30^\circ\text{C}$ and slowly oxidizes in air to emit greenish-white light (chemiluminescence).
Red and black phosphorus have polymeric layered/network structures that relieve this angular strain, making them much less reactive.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Neil Bartlett first prepared an authentic noble gas compound, $\text{Xe}^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$, based on the observation that:
options: Molecular oxygen and xenon have almost identical first ionization enthalpies
Platinum hexafluoride oxidizes fluorine gas to ozone
Xenon has a larger atomic radius than radon
Xenon and argon have identical crystal structures
questions.solution:
In 1962, Neil Bartlett observed that platinum hexafluoride ($\text{PtF}_6$), a powerful oxidizing agent, oxidized molecular oxygen to form an ionic red compound:
$$\text{O}_2 + \text{PtF}_6 \rightarrow \text{O}_2^+[\text{PtF}_6]^- = [\text{O}_2]^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$$
He recognized that:
1. The first ionization enthalpy of molecular oxygen ($1175\text{ kJ/mol}$) is nearly identical to that of xenon ($1170\text{ kJ/mol}$).
2. The molecular diameter of $\text{O}_2$ is very similar to the atomic diameter of $\text{Xe}$.
Bartlett reasoned that $\text{PtF}_6$ should also oxidize xenon, successfully synthesizing the first noble gas compound: $\text{Xe}^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$, an orange-yellow solid.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The basicity and the oxidation state of phosphorus in hypophosphorous acid (phosphinic acid, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) are respectively:
questions.solution:
Structure of hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$):
- Central phosphorus atom has tetrahedral coordination with:
  - One oxo-oxygen ($\text{P}=\text{O}$ double bond)
  - One hydroxyl group ($\text{P}-\text{OH}$ single bond)
  - Two direct hydridic bonds (two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds)
1. Basicity is determined exclusively by the number of ionizable protons (protons attached to oxygen as $-\text{OH}$ groups). Because there is only one $-\text{OH}$ group, the acid is monobasic (basicity $= 1$).
2. Oxidation state of phosphorus:
$$3(+1) + x + 2(-2) = 0 \implies 3 + x - 4 = 0 \implies x = +1$$
Thus, basicity is $1$ and the oxidation state is $+1$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The correct order of reducing power for Group 15 hydrides is:
questions.solution:
Reducing character of a hydride is governed by the ease with which it gives up hydrogen, which depends inversely on the $E-\text{H}$ bond dissociation enthalpy:
1. As atomic size increases down Group 15 ($\text{N} < \text{P} < \text{As} < \text{Sb} < \text{Bi}$), the $E-\text{H}$ bond length increases and bond energy decreases.
2. $\text{BiH}_3$ has the weakest $E-\text{H}$ bond, decomposes rapidly at room temperature, and is the strongest reducing agent in the group.
3. $\text{NH}_3$ has the shortest and strongest bond and is only a mild reducing agent.
Hence, reducing power increases down the group:
$$\text{BiH}_3 > \text{SbH}_3 > \text{AsH}_3 > \text{PH}_3 > \text{NH}_3$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In the contact process for the commercial manufacture of sulfuric acid, sulfur trioxide ($\text{SO}_3$) is dissolved in concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ rather than directly in water because:
options: Direct addition to water is violently exothermic and forms a dense, unmanageable acid fog (mist)
Direct reaction with water yields an equilibrium with low percent conversion
questions.solution:
The direct dissolution of $\text{SO}_3$ in water:
$$\text{SO}_3(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(l); \quad \Delta H = -133\text{ kJ/mol}$$
is extremely exothermic.
1. The intense heat released instantaneously vaporizes water and produces an aerosol of microscopic sulfuric acid droplets that forms a thick, corrosive, and unmanageable acid mist that cannot be readily condensed.
2. Instead, $\text{SO}_3$ is absorbed smoothly in $98\%$ concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form oleum (pyrosulfuric acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$):
$$\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$$
Oleum is subsequently diluted with the calculated amount of water to yield sulfuric acid of desired concentration.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Among the interhalogen compounds, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Interhalogen compounds are generally less reactive than the parent elemental halogens (except $\text{F}_2$)
They are covalent molecules and are diamagnetic in nature
In $XX'_n$ compounds, $X$ is always the larger halogen with lower electronegativity
Hydrolysis of an interhalogen compound always produces a halide ion derived from the smaller halogen and a hypohalite/halate from the larger halogen
questions.solution:
1. In an interhalogen molecule $X-X'$, the bond between two different halogens is polar and generally weaker than the homonuclear $X-X$ bond in elemental halogens (except the $\text{F}-\text{F}$ bond in $\text{F}_2$).
2. Consequently, interhalogen compounds are **more reactive** than elemental halogens (with the sole exception of $\text{F}_2$).
Statement A is incorrect because it falsely claims interhalogens are less reactive.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The transition temperature at which rhombic sulfur ($\alpha$-sulfur) and monoclinic sulfur ($\beta$-sulfur) exist in dynamic equilibrium with each other at $1\text{ atm}$ pressure is:
questions.solution:
Sulfur exhibits enantiotropic allotropy:
1. Below $369\text{ K}$ ($95.6^\circ\text{C} \approx 96^\circ\text{C}$), rhombic ($\alpha$) sulfur is the thermodynamically stable crystalline modification.
2. Above $369\text{ K}$, monoclinic ($\beta$) sulfur is the thermodynamically stable allotrope.
3. At exactly $369\text{ K}$, both crystalline allotropic modifications coexist in equilibrium:
$$\alpha\text{-Sulfur} \xrightleftharpoons{369\text{ K}} \beta\text{-Sulfur}$$
This specific equilibrium temperature is known as the **transition temperature**.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The correct order of boiling points for the noble gases is:
questions.solution:
Noble gases exist as monatomic gases held together solely by weak London dispersion forces (instantaneous dipole-induced dipole attractions):
1. Down Group 18, atomic size and the number of electrons increase from $\text{He}$ to $\text{Xe}$.
2. The larger electron cloud is more polarizable, which strengthens dispersion forces.
3. Stronger intermolecular dispersion forces require higher thermal energy to overcome, resulting in a continuous increase in boiling points down the group:
$$\text{He} (4.2\text{ K}) < \text{Ne} (27.1\text{ K}) < \text{Ar} (87.3\text{ K}) < \text{Kr} (119.9\text{ K}) < \text{Xe} (165.0\text{ K})$$

questions.question: Which of the following oxoacids of sulfur contains an $\text{O}-\text{O}$ peroxo linkage?
questions.solution:
Structural features of sulfur oxoacids:
- $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$ (Peroxodisulfuric acid / Marshall's acid): Has the structure $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{SO}_2-\text{OH}$. The two sulfur centers are connected by a peroxo linkage ($-\text{O}-\text{O}-$).
- $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$ (Oleum / Pyrosulfuric acid): Contains an oxo bridge ($\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}$).
- $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_6$ (Dithionic acid): Contains a direct $\text{S}-\text{S}$ single bond.
- $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ (Thiosulfuric acid): Contains a terminal $\text{S}=\text{S}$ bond.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The correct order of acidic strength for the oxoacids of chlorine is:
questions.solution:
Acidic strength of oxoacids of the same element increases with the oxidation state of the central atom:
- $\text{HClO}$: oxidation state of $\text{Cl} = +1$
- $\text{HClO}_2$: oxidation state of $\text{Cl} = +3$
- $\text{HClO}_3$: oxidation state of $\text{Cl} = +5$
- $\text{HClO}_4$: oxidation state of $\text{Cl} = +7$
As the number of terminal electronegative oxo-oxygen atoms increases from $0$ in $\text{ClO}^-$ to $3$ in $\text{ClO}_4^-$, the negative charge of the conjugate base is increasingly dispersed over more oxygen atoms via resonance delocalization.
The perchlorate anion ($\text{ClO}_4^-$) is exceptionally stable due to delocalization over four equivalent oxygen atoms, making perchloric acid ($\text{HClO}_4$) the strongest acid:
$$\text{HClO} < \text{HClO}_2 < \text{HClO}_3 < \text{HClO}_4$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Why is dinitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) chemically unreactive and inert at room temperature?
options: Very high bond dissociation energy of the $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond ($945\text{ kJ/mol}$)
questions.solution:
Dinitrogen consists of two nitrogen atoms joined by a triple bond ($1\ \sigma$ and $2\ \pi$ bonds) with an extremely short bond length ($109.8\text{ pm}$).
Because of effective $2p\pi-2p\pi$ overlap, the bond dissociation enthalpy of the $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ bond is extraordinarily large:
$$\Delta H_{\text{diss}} = 945.4\text{ kJ/mol}$$
This tremendous activation barrier renders dinitrogen virtually inert at room temperature, requiring high temperatures and catalysts to undergo chemical reactions.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The hybridization and molecular shape of xenon oxytetrafluoride ($\text{XeOF}_4$) are respectively:
questions.solution:
For $\text{XeOF}_4$:
- Valence electrons of Xenon $= 8$
- Xenon forms $4$ single bonds with Fluorine $\implies 4\ \sigma$ bond pairs
- Xenon forms $1$ double bond with Oxygen $\implies 1\ \sigma$ bond pair ($+ 1\ \pi$ bond)
- Total $\sigma$ bonding pairs $= 4 + 1 = 5$
- Electrons utilized in $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds $= 4\ (\text{with F}) + 2\ (\text{with O}) = 6$
- Remaining non-bonding electrons $= 8 - 6 = 2 \implies 1\text{ lone pair}$
- Steric number $= 5\ (\sigma\text{ bonds}) + 1\ (\text{lone pair}) = 6 \implies sp^3d^2$ hybridization.
- Octahedral electron arrangement with $1$ axial lone pair and the $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ double bond trans to it produces a square pyramidal molecular geometry.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] When chlorine water is exposed to sunlight for an extended period, it loses its greenish-yellow color due to the formation of:
questions.solution:
When chlorine dissolves in water, it forms an equilibrium mixture of hydrochloric acid and hypochlorous acid:
$$\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HCl} + \text{HOCl}$$
On exposure to sunlight, the unstable hypochlorous acid ($\text{HOCl}$) undergoes photolytic decomposition to produce hydrochloric acid and nascent/molecular oxygen:
$$2\text{HOCl} \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2\text{HCl} + \text{O}_2 \uparrow$$
Net photochemical reaction:
$$2\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 4\text{HCl} + \text{O}_2$$
Because dissolved $\text{Cl}_2$ is converted into colorless $\text{HCl}(aq)$ and $\text{O}_2(g)$, the greenish-yellow solution turns completely colorless.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following nitrogen oxides is a colored gas and paramagnetic in nature?
questions.solution:
Examine the properties of nitrogen oxides:
1. Nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$):
- Total valence electrons $= 5\ (\text{N}) + 2(6)\ (\text{O}) = 17\text{ electrons}$ (odd electron molecule).
- Possesses one unpaired electron, making it paramagnetic.
- Absorbs blue light, imparting a distinct reddish-brown color.
2. $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ (laughing gas): Colorless, diamagnetic ($16e^-$).
3. $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$: Colorless solid/liquid, diamagnetic dimer of $\text{NO}_2$.
4. $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$: Colorless solid, diamagnetic.
Thus, $\text{NO}_2$ is colored and paramagnetic.

questions.question: The bleaching action of sulfur dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$) differs from that of chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$) because:
options: $\text{SO}_2$ bleaches by temporary reduction, whereas $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches permanently by oxidation
$\text{SO}_2$ bleaches permanently by oxidation, whereas $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches by reduction
questions.solution:
1. Sulfur dioxide bleaches in the presence of moisture through a **reduction** mechanism:
$$\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2[\text{H}]$$
The nascent hydrogen reduces colored organic matter to colorless products. On subsequent exposure to atmospheric oxygen, the bleached material is re-oxidized back to its colored form, making the bleaching action temporary.
2. Chlorine bleaches in the presence of water through an **oxidation** mechanism by releasing nascent oxygen:
$$\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl} + [\text{O}]$$
$$\text{Colored matter} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{Colorless oxidized product}$$
This oxidative degradation is irreversible and permanent.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In which of the following compounds does xenon have an oxidation state of $+4$?
questions.solution:
Calculate the oxidation state of xenon in each compound:
- In $\text{XeF}_2$: $x + 2(-1) = 0 \implies x = +2$
- In $\text{XeF}_4$: $x + 4(-1) = 0 \implies x = +4$
- In $\text{XeF}_6$: $x + 6(-1) = 0 \implies x = +6$
- In $\text{XeO}_3$: $x + 3(-2) = 0 \implies x = +6$
Thus, xenon has an oxidation state of $+4$ in $\text{XeF}_4$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Heating white phosphorus with concentrated aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ solution in an inert atmosphere of $\text{CO}_2$ produces:
questions.solution:
White phosphorus undergoes disproportionation when boiled with concentrated caustic soda ($\text{NaOH}$) solution in an inert atmosphere:
$$\text{P}_4 + 3\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{PH}_3 \uparrow + 3\text{NaH}_2\text{PO}_2$$
1. Phosphorus in $\text{P}_4$ has an oxidation state of $0$.
2. It is reduced to $-3$ in phosphine ($\text{PH}_3$).
3. It is simultaneously oxidized to $+1$ in sodium hypophosphite ($\text{NaH}_2\text{PO}_2$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Calculate the total number of lone pairs of electrons present on the central xenon atom in a molecule of xenon difluoride ($\text{XeF}_2$).
questions.solution:
In $\text{XeF}_2$:
- Xenon has $8$ valence electrons.
- It forms $2$ single $\text{Xe}-\text{F}$ covalent bonds.
- Non-bonding electrons $= 8 - 2 = 6$.
$$\text{Number of lone pairs} = \frac{6}{2} = 3.0$$
(These three lone pairs occupy equatorial positions in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry, giving a linear molecule).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Find the number of $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bonds present in one molecule of pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$).
questions.solution:
Pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$) is formed by the condensation of two molecules of orthophosphoric acid with the elimination of one water molecule:
$$\text{HO}_2\text{P}(=\text{O})-\text{O}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$$
Its structure contains:
- Two terminal $\text{P}=\text{O}$ double bonds
- One bridging $\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}$ linkage
- Four ionizable hydroxyl groups (four $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bonds, making it tetrabasic)
Thus, the number of $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bonds is $4.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Find the oxidation state of sulfur in Marshall's acid (peroxodisulfuric acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$).
questions.solution:
Structure of $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$:
$$\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{SO}_2-\text{OH}$$
There are $6$ normal oxo/hydroxyl oxygen atoms (oxidation state $-2$) and $2$ peroxo oxygen atoms forming the central peroxo bridge (oxidation state $-1$):
$$2(+1) + 2x + 6(-2) + 2(-1) = 0$$
$$2 + 2x - 12 - 2 = 0$$
$$2x - 12 = 0 \implies 2x = 12 \implies x = +6.0$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In the cyclic trimer of sulfur trioxide, $(\text{SO}_3)_3$ (also written as $\text{S}_3\text{O}_9$), calculate the total number of $\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}$ bridging bonds.
questions.solution:
The structure of solid cyclic sulfur trioxide trimer ($\gamma$-$\text{SO}_3$ or $\text{S}_3\text{O}_9$) is a puckered six-membered ring containing alternating sulfur and oxygen atoms:
$$\dots-\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}-\text{O}-\dots$$
Each of the three sulfur atoms is bonded to two terminal double-bonded oxo-oxygen atoms ($=\text{O}$) and linked to two neighboring sulfur atoms via oxygen bridges.
Thus, the cyclic ring contains exactly $3.0$ bridging $\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}$ bonds.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Among the following oxoacids: $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2, \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3, \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4, \text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$, how many can act as reducing agents due to the presence of direct $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds?
questions.solution:
Oxoacids of phosphorus containing direct $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds have strong reducing properties:
1. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ (hypophosphorous acid): has two direct $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds $\implies$ strong reducing agent.
2. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ (phosphorous acid): has one direct $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bond $\implies$ good reducing agent.
3. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ (orthophosphoric acid): has zero $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds (all hydrogens are in $-\text{OH}$ groups) $\implies$ non-reducing.
4. $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$ (pyrophosphoric acid): has zero $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds $\implies$ non-reducing.
Total number of reducing oxoacids $= 2.0$ ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ and $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$).
